title: Fylgja bundle manifest v4 — per-platform forwarding, bootstrap delivery, intent’s enabled state per row
description: From M6’s v2 (specs/006-psp-lossy-mapping/contracts/manifest.schema.json): bundle_version was 3 at M7 (FR-025; D-025 and its M6 notes) and is 4 at M12 (FR-005, below). `fidelity.production_forwarding` is an object, one entry per platform in the bundle keyed by its package id, so a mixed bundle asserts each platform’s forwarding and M1’s fidelity.forwarding.mixed refusal retires; `mapping[].node_name` is on every row (null on a row without a port) and `fidelity.lossy` is always present ([] when empty), ending M6’s one exception to the empty-list rule; every node gains `bootstrap` {file, via}: the bootstrap file the bundle carries for it and whether containerlab applies it at deploy (startup_config, the topology names it) or the push sends its lines before the artifact’s (push, the topology node has no startup-config; M7 research R4). A v2 or v1 bundle is refused by `twin provision` as bundle.version.unsupported naming both versions. Everything else is v2’s. From M5’s v2 (specs/005-configuration/contracts/manifest.schema.json), bundle_version still 2 (M6 FR-017): a mapping row may carry `node_name`, the node’s own name for its port, present only where it differs from `interface`; `fidelity.lossy` records every lossy mapping and every shared port, present only when it has content; omissions gain the rule omit.interface.shared. Both fields are the one deliberate exception to M1’s rule that every empty list is emitted as []: a bundle with nothing lossy in it is byte-identical to M5’s, so the goldens and both fixture ids stand and no following twin is rebuilt by the upgrade. The exception expires with M7’s bundle_version bump for per-platform forwarding (D-025), which makes both fields unconditional in the same move. From v1 (specs/001-read-compile/contracts/manifest.schema.json): bundle_version is 2, and every node gains `artifact`, the configuration file the bundle carries for it beside its bootstrap (M5 FR-001–FR-005; research R8). A v1 bundle is refused by `twin provision` as bundle.version.unsupported naming both versions (FR-003). Nothing of Infrahub’s — artifact, storage or definition identifiers, a time of generation — appears (FR-005), so bundle_id moves for the artifact’s bytes or name and for nothing else. Everything else is v1’s. M12 (FR-005): bundle_version is 4. Every mapping row carries enabled, the interface's intent admin state (the CTM's enabled, true when unset), so the bundle says what intent says of each port: twin verify asserts nothing of a cabled port whose row says false, and records the skip. The topology, the bootstrap and every configs file are unchanged by the field.

provenance.description: The provenance block: the intent's address, copied from the CTM envelope minus `observed_at`. Nothing about the read, the host, the clock or the build.

at.description: Present iff the operator supplied --at; verbatim.

management_port.description: Always the PSP's interfaces.management name: containerlab gives every node one, whether or not intent flags a mgmt_only interface.

artifact.description: The node’s configuration artifact, as the bundle carries it: `file` is its path in the bundle, configs/<node>.<artifact_name>, bytes exactly as Infrahub served them; `checksum` is Infrahub’s own (MD5 hex: R6), verbatim; `size` is the byte count.

bootstrap.description: M7: the node’s bootstrap file, rendered from its package’s template (Constitution IV), and how it reaches the node (the package’s config.bootstrap_via).

mapping.description: One row per interface in intent. Sorted by (device, interface). M7: `node_name` on every row. M12: `enabled` on every row.

port.description: Node port; null when omitted or configured-not-cabled without a port

node_name.description: M7 (FR-025): on every row. The node’s own name for the port, as the profile’s rule renders it, equal to `interface` where the platform keeps the production name; null on a row without a port.

enabled.description: M12 (FR-005): the interface's intent admin state (ctm.Interface.enabled, true when unset). On every row from bundle 4. A cabled row with false is still cabled and its bootstrap still enables the port; intent's disabling reaches the node through the artifact (M5 research R5), and twin verify asserts nothing of the port or its link.

links.description: Cabled links only. Sorted by id.

omissions.description: Everything left out and why. Sorted by object then rule. Never empty when the mapping has an 'omitted' row. M6: omit.interface.shared is an uncabled interface whose port a cabled interface of the same device holds (FR-015); omit.interface.unmappable’s reason now names the rule, placeholder, value and range when a rule matched out of range (FR-019).

fidelity.description: Asserted, never measured (D-022); `basis` says so in the bundle itself (Constitution X). M7: `production_forwarding` per platform; `lossy` always present.

basis.description: Fidelity is asserted from PSP data and compiler decisions, never measured against production. The only value at M1; a verification layer would add another.

production_forwarding.description: M7 (FR-025; D-025): one entry per platform in the bundle, keyed by nodes[].psp.id, holding that package’s fidelity.production_forwarding. Keys sorted. Where production forwards in software the twin’s data plane is a fair guide; where in hardware it is not (architecture §1).

lossy.description: M6 (FR-016), unconditional from M7 (FR-025): one entry per interface a lossy rule mapped, and per interface whose port another interface of the same device also renders to, whichever rule; [] when there is none. Sorted by (device, interface). `port` is the rendered port even for an interface the mapping table shows omitted for sharing; `shares` lists every other interface of the device rendering to the port, sorted by interface, with its rule and whether it is cabled. Asserted, like the rest of the block.

node_name.description: the node’s own name for the port, whether or not it differs from the production name

rule.description: the rule’s name (FR-021), never its position or pattern

lossy.description: whether that rule is declared lossy; false only for an interface recorded because its port is shared
